title: Banning Foreign Pharmacies from Sponsored Search: The Online Consumer Response
authors: Matthew William Chesnes; Weijia Dai; Ginger Zhe Jin
eligible_reason: Not a staggered design. Google's ban on non-NABP pharmacies from sponsored search is a single common date for all treated websites, followed by a second common regime change. Treatment groups are certification tiers (multi-valued). The main estimator is synthetic control (Table 7, Tables 10-13 Panels A-B). The two-part model uses logit plus a conditional-on-positive xtreg with tier x regime interactions. The main comScore click data are not shipped.
design_notes: two_part_model/main.do: Table 6 pre-trend tests (logit and xtreg with tier x linear trend). Table 8: logit positive ~ tier2 tier3 Ireg1 tier2Xreg1 tier3Xreg1 Ireg2 tier2Xreg2 tier3Xreg2, plus xtreg ln(clicks) on the same regressors if clicks>0, fe cluster(site_id). Regime dummies are common dates (the transition months 2010m2 and 2011m8 are dropped). Tables 10-13 Panel C repeat this by heterogeneity bins. The ATE/ and HTE_*/ folders run synth for each treated website against untreated websites, with placebo inference.
software_notes: Stata 14.2 with synth; MATLAB for placebo draws.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The comScore website-month click files that the README lists as main data are absent. Only auxiliary and placebo-output files are shipped.
